## Beast (how seats in this repo coordinate)

@@TWIN@@

Protocol: @@PROTOCOL@@ `docs/protocol.md`. Scripts: `@@SCRIPTS@@`. @@DECIDER_NAME@@ reads one board: the issue titled "Pending decisions (generated)" in `@@BOARD@@`, and https://github.com/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3Adecision%2Cneeds-review+assignee%3A@@DECIDER@@ . There is no standing intermediary: a seat files its own rows, posts its own status, and messages another seat only at a seam (`seats.sh address <SEAT>`).

Seats in this repo:
@@SEATS@@

**Your home.** Each seat's sessions run in its own home (`seat.sh where <SEAT>`): the checkout, a worktree `<repo>.seats/<LABEL>` on branch `seat/<LABEL>`, or a wrapper `~/.beast/homes/<login>/<LABEL>` opened with its `claude.sh`. A session started in a home is told its seat by the plugin's SessionStart hook. A new seat is made with `seat.sh new <LABEL> --role "<text>" --tracking <owner/repo#N>`, which prints how to open it.

**At every session start, and after any reload or compaction:** `join.sh <SEAT>` from your home (records your address, regenerates this block, lists memory files that duplicate GitHub state), which ends by printing `resume.sh <SEAT>`: your last handoff, your notes and your inbox. Then re-read this file. A long inbox or a handoff to draft: hire the `seat-clerk` agent, which drafts and never posts.

**Before a compaction or a shutdown:** `status.sh <your tracking issue> --seat <SEAT> --state handoff --next "<next act>" --text "<state, waiting on, branches, gotchas>"`.

**Board or desk.** Ask: would a development team put this on a PR or an issue for the lead's approval? Yes → the board: a code change is the PR itself, `pr.sh request <pr> --seat <SEAT>` (merge on their approve with `pr.sh close <pr> --merge --words … --record … --by <SEAT>`, `--rejected` on reject); an act without code (deploy PROD, release, spend, chain, secrets, scope, a design approval) is a decision row. No, it is a question across the desk (a name, a rewording, which option, a clarification) → your desk: `desk.sh ask <SEAT> --text "…" [--options "a | b"] [--default a]`; words they type to you for an ask go on with `desk.sh answer <SEAT> <n> "<verbatim>"`; a durable note to another seat is `desk.sh msg <TO> --from <SEAT> --text "…"`. The desk never touches the board. Every row, desk, status, note and ack is written in a private repo: the scripts refuse a public or public-intended one, naming where to write instead.

**The board is a queue.** Anything you wait on from @@DECIDER_NAME@@ is a row filed BEFORE you ask them: `decision.sh new --assignee @@DECIDER@@ --seat <SEAT> [--decides <owner/repo>] …` (six sections). It files in your home repo (the roster `repo`); `--decides` names the repo it decides in the row's Decision section. The row stays open until their word, and you close on it with `decision.sh close <row> --words … --record … --by <SEAT>`. `decision.sh record … --words "<verbatim>" --record "<commit — path>" --by <SEAT>` files and closes in one act, and is ONLY for a significant word (scope, engine, ship-or-cut, release) @@DECIDER_NAME@@ already gave in session before any row existed; never for something you are about to ask. A minor word (wording, copy, a link) goes only into the repo's dated record. At each wake run `decision.sh inbox <SEAT>` (board rows, then your desk; computed from GitHub, nothing local) and ack what you act on: `ack.sh <row or desk> --seat <SEAT> --state seen|executed|blocked --next "<act>"`. Status goes on your tracking issue at a blocker, a completion or a seam, never a tick.

**Milestones.** Set out your milestones at the start of a workstream (`workstream.sh new --milestone "<title>|<YYYY-MM-DD>|<what it delivers>"`, or `milestone.sh new`). Every row, desk ask and PR names one (`--milestone "<title>"`; the scripts refuse one without it while the repo has an open milestone). Declare what you wait on as data with `--waits-on <seat | owner/repo#N>` on `decision.sh new`, `desk.sh ask` and `milestone.sh new`; `deps.sh <SEAT>` shows each as released, delayed, changed direction or waiting. Move a milestone with a why (`milestone.sh move <title> --due <date> --why "…"`) rather than letting it go stale. At a close (`milestone.sh close <title> [--carry <next>]`), send each participant their section with `report.sh milestone <title> --post --by <SEAT>`.

**Wrap-up.** A milestone ends with a wrap-up, so spent decisions and traffic do not pile up on the board: `wrapup.sh plan <M>` lists what will be deleted and posts nothing; `wrapup.sh request <M> --seat <SEAT>` files one row approved with `wrap up <M>`; fold the milestone's closed rows into the docs with the realign skill (`wrapup.sh brief <M>`; ONE commit whose message cites each folded row's url, and `dropped: <url> — <why>` lines in `.beast/wrapup/<slug>/fold-in.md` for the rest); then, on their word, `wrapup.sh run <M> --words "<verbatim>" --by <SEAT> --fold-in <sha>` publishes the release notes, deletes what the plan lists, closes the milestone and prints the KB syncs to run. The decider's words live on their row until the wrap-up folds them in; no separate record file is needed.

**Where state lives.** Your role: this repo's agent definitions and CLAUDE.md. Your working state: your newest handoff on your tracking issue, never in auto-memory. What you must not relearn on another surface: your notes, one `BEAST-NOTES` comment on your tracking issue (`notes.sh <SEAT> show|set --text-file <f>|append --text "<line>"`). Your home's auto-memory: lessons about this repo only. Two seats never share a home.
